issues.description: The template exports the program entry symbol as 'main' (global main in pixel.asm), but the solution file declares 'global _start' while still defining a 'main' label. This mismatch of exported/global entry symbols is inconsistent across template and solution and may confuse students about which symbol to provide or cause linking differences depending on the build/link process.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the exported/global symbol consistent. Either change the solution to export 'main' (use 'global main') or change the template/Makefile and problem text to expect '_start'. Preferably use 'global main' in the solution to match the template and typical gcc linking expectations.

issues.description: The program entry symbol is declared inconsistently: the template file declares the entry as 'global main' while the solution file declares 'global _start'. This mismatched global label for the same conceptual program entry point can confuse students (and tooling) about which symbol is required/expected when assembling and linking the program, since the Makefile and template imply 'main' is the intended entry symbol.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent entry symbol across artifacts. Either change the solution to declare 'global main' (matching the template and Makefile expectation) or update the template and Makefile to expect '_start' consistently. Preferably align the solution to 'global main' so students can directly run the provided template/Makefile without confusion.
